title: Long session: explain, build, test and expose a concurrency limit
prompts: I'm new to this codebase. Walk me through what happens, step by step, from `scheduler.scheduleJob(job)` until the job's handler has run and the job is finished, including what happens when the handler throws. Cite the files and functions involved. Don't change anything yet.

Now add a per-queue concurrency limit. `new Queue({ concurrency: n })` takes a positive integer (default 1, which is today's behaviour) and exposes it as `queue.concurrency`; invalid values (zero, negative, non-integer, not a number) must throw. A `Worker` must run up to `queue.concurrency` jobs of that queue at the same time, never more, still taking jobs in priority order. `runUntilIdle()` must resolve only when no job is ready and none is still running. A failing job frees its slot.
Add tests for it in test/concurrency.test.js: the limit is respected, priority order is kept, a failure frees the slot, and invalid values throw. Run the suite.

Expose it in the CLI: `taskflow worker --concurrency N`. `parseArgs` in src/cli/index.js reads it as a number and throws an Error that mentions "concurrency" for an invalid value; the worker command applies it to the queue before it runs the jobs. Document the option in README.md.
notes: Four prompts in ONE session (each resumes the previous one): explain, implement, test, expose. A long session re-reads its growing context on every call, which is where cache-read cost, and so any saving from smaller reads, accumulates. Only the final state is graded.
